bug_report_content:
id: 381
status: Fixed
summary: division by zero wrongly throws JSC_DIVIDE_BY_0_ERROR
labels: ['Type-Defect', 'Priority-Medium']
stars: 2
commentCount: 6
Comment 0 (2011-03-15): What steps will reproduce the problem? unaliased division by zero `1/0` What is the expected output? What do you see instead? I expect minified code, but an error is thrown instead. What version of the product are you using? On what operating system? appspot Please provide any additional information below. Division by zero is a perfectly sane operation in ECMAScript. See 11.5.2 [0] of the ECMAScript 5 specification. Aliased division by zero `(n=1)/0` is permitted. [0] http://es5.github.com/#x11.5.2
Comment 1 (2011-03-15): In what way does this cause a problem? Generally, devision by zero is indicative of a programming error. We could make it suppressible however.
Comment 2 (2011-03-15): In ES3, `Infinity` is a writable variable, just like `undefined`. For these cases it's both safer and faster to generate the value rather than look for it in the scope chain. Because of this, `1/0`, `1/-0`, and `void 0` are common JS idioms.
Comment 3 (2011-03-16): i also think this is a dumb error and has never solved any real problem.
Comment 5 (2011-03-18): This issue was closed by revision r900.
